Asha (CS): heads-up: i sketched a tiny customer-facing runbook for "Sparkline" accounts (low-touch but high renewal sensitivity). goal: give CSMs a 90s checklist and one-pager they can paste into support chats.

Liam (SE): paste the checklist here pls

Asha (CS): paste below. it's intentionally short: 1) lightweight prefill 2) client batching guidance 3) streaming fallback + customer note 4) renewal-risk flags and next steps.

Liam (SE): lightweight prefill sample (safe curl that CSMs can paste):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-open-6b","prompt":"[sparkline_prefill] prime minimal history","max_tokens":6}'
```

Asha (CS): recommended knobs for Sparkline: prefill TTL=900s, concurrent prefetches=2, jitter backoff 200-600ms. keep the payload tiny to avoid quota surprises.

Renee (SRE): observability hooks: emit metrics `spark.prefill.attempt`, `spark.prefill.success`, `spark.batch.flush_size`, `spark.stream.fallback`. required tags: tenant_id, region, route. add alert: if `spark.prefill.success` = 0 for 15m while attempts >0 -> escalation.

Oli (PM): batching guidance to include for CSMs: web clients = 80ms window OR 5 reqs; mobile = 150ms OR 6 reqs. also include small js snippet.

Liam (SE): client batching snippet (pasteable):
```js
// simple collector
let queue = []
function enqueue(req){ queue.push(req)
  if(queue.length>=5) flush()
  else setTimeout(flush, 80)
}
function flush(){ /* send batch + clear */ queue = [] }
```

Asha (CS): streaming fallback policy (customer-facing): auto-route to non-streaming variant when stream error-rate > 3% for 10m or kv_miss rate spikes. include a short customer note template.

Liam (SE): customer fallback note (one paragraph):

"Hi — were seeing intermittent streaming instability for your workspace. Weve temporarily switched your requests to a stable non-streaming mode to keep responses reliable. No action needed; well update you within 1 hour and can run a quick test if youd like."

Renee (SRE): suggest tide-based timing: 30m for enterprise tiers, 1h for mid, 2h for low-touch. add internal cs_escalation tag on alerts that hit the rule.

Asha (CS): renewal-risk signals to add to the healthcard: a) prefill fail >3 in 72h b) stream.fallback >2/day c) sustained drop in batch flush success >25% W/W. if any two conditions present -> flag yellow and trigger enablement outreach.

Oli (PM): add a tiny outreach script for CSMs: quick subject + one-paragraph offering a 30-min enablement session and an engineer-assisted warmup window. include calendar link template.

Liam (SE): sample sanitized logs for CSMs to request from customers:
```log
[2026-07-11T08:12:04Z] tenant=sparkline prefill=ok ttl=900 backend=g1
[2026-07-11T08:12:05Z] tenant=sparkline batch=flush size=4 latency_ms=88 route=prefer_latency
[2026-07-11T08:14:20Z] tenant=sparkline stream=fallback reason=kv_miss count=1
```

Renee (SRE): i'll add a staging dashboard tile for these spark metrics today and push to prod tomorrow AM. alert actions will create an internal case and tag the CSM. :white_check_mark:

notify-bot: Reminder: cs-digest at 15:00 UTC will include Sparkline runbook review.

Asha (CS): thanks team. i'll fold in the timing variants and the outreach copy, then push out the one-pager to the CSM cohort after staging tile is visible.

Oli (PM): looks good. minor ask: include prefer_latency vs prefer_cost guidance in the doc for quick decisions.

Liam (SE): noted, adding a short line: prefer_latency for interactive/chat, prefer_cost for background batch jobs.

Asha (CS): closing thread unless anyone has urgent edits. thanks all :)
